podcast.body: Considered by rap historians to be the highlight of the Bridge Wars, this 1987 BDP single is described as a "bouncy piano-based boom-bap jam." It gained significant influence, being "sampled by dozens of other rap tracks" in the future. Despite its "pop-friendly allusion" through interpolation of Billy Joel's "It's Still Rock and Roll to Me" and high praise from connoisseurs, the song did not make the national charts. "Rap historians generally agree that the highlight of the beef was the 1987 BDP single The Bridge is over, a bouncy piano-based boom-bap jam that would go on to be sampled by dozens of other rap tracks."
